NFL injury tracker Week 7: Latest news, fantasy implications as Saquon Barkley (hamstring), Lamar Jackson (ankle) return to practice; Puka Nacua (calf) limited

Week 7 is underway, and we're tracking all the injuries before game time.

NFC North: Bears (played Thurs.) | Lions | Packers | Vikings

NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers

NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

Live injury updates

Two star players who have each missed the past two weeks were back at practice for their respective teams.

The Philadelphia Eagles welcomed back Saquon Barkley after he's been out since Week 4 due to a hamstring injury. If all goes well, the running back is in line to play when the Eagles host the Dallas Cowboys on "Monday Night Football."

Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson was also back on the practice field after sitting two games with an ankle injury. He was limited for a second straight day on Thursday, but took part in drills ahead of Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals.

There was a worrying sign for the Los Angeles Rams on Thursday as wide receiver Puka Nacua left practice with a calf injury. He was listed as limited three days before the Rams, who will already be without wideout Davante Adams (hamstring), face the Las Vegas Raiders.

Nacua has already missed two games this season with a psoas injury.

Other Week 7 injuries to monitor:

San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) and defensive end Nick Bosa (knee/calf) did not practice on Thursday. Bosa has not practiced for almost a month after pulling his calf in practice and has already missed four games with the injury.

New York Jets running back Breece Hall (quad) returned to practice on Thursday. While he was a limited participant, it's an encouraging sign for Hall, who has missed three games with the injury. He is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.

The Arizona Cardinals are not expecting to have Jeremiyah Love (ankle) available to them this week against the Denver Broncos. The running back will reportedly be sidelined for a second straight game. Head coach Mike LaFleur told the media last week that an injured reserve stint had not been discussed for Love.

Baker Mayfield (thumb) is expected to return this week for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The quarterback has been out since injuring the digit in Week 3. He will not have Emeka Egbuka as one of his available weapons. The wide receiver was at practice on Friday, but remains in concussion protocol and is out for Sunday.

While the Houston Texans likely won't have running back David Montgomery (groin) against the New York Giants, they will be getting back Tank Dell. The wide receiver has not played since suffering a serious knee injury in Dec. 2024. Nearly 22 months later, the 2023 third-round draft pick said he's feeling back to his old self. "I'm anxious to get back out there and play some football," he said.

Chiefs placing Josh Simmons on IR after LT resurfaced at practice, say he needs more time to 'return to full function'

Patrick Mahomes will have to keep playing without his expected blindside protector for a while longer. In the lead-up to a Week 7 "Sunday Night Football" road game against the Seattle Seahawks, the 5-0 Kansas City Chiefs are placing left tackle Josh Simmons on injured reserve, Rick Burkholder announced on Thursday.

Burkholder, the team's vice president of sports medicine and performance, provided reporters with a detailed timeline of Simmons' bulging herniated disc in his lumbar spine, a back injury that's kept the second-year pro sidelined all season.

In the process, Burkholder, now in his 14th season with the Chiefs, explained that, while Simmons returned to practice in a limited capacity last week, Kansas City's medical staff didn't deem the 2025 No. 32 overall pick ready for game action.

"We feel that he's plateaued in the rehab process as he's trying to get to the final steps of recovery with return to competition, and he's just not there yet," Burkholder said. "After discussion with Josh yesterday, we gave him some time to talk with his family and his representatives to investigate next steps as he goes through this process."

That's why Simmons was listed with both "personal" and "back" next to his name on the team's injury report after not practicing on Wednesday, Burkholder clarified.

Simmons was allowed the day off to congregate with his family and agent. Burkholder said everyone, including Simmons and head coach Andy Reid, agreed that Simmons should be put on IR "to give him more time to return to full function."

At this point, Simmons' back injury still doesn't require surgery, according to Burkholder.

Mays' return gives Detroit the proverbial nice problem to have. Juice Scruggs, acquired in the trade that sent David Montgomery to the Houston Texans, has played well at center. As Mays works his way back, the two may alternate at the position with Scruggs also getting snaps at left guard.

title: Anton Harrison injury: Jaguars LT out for season after surgery reveals torn ACL - CBS Sports
description:
27 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, Harrison moved from right tackle to left tackle this offseason.
The bad news, outside the obvious bad news that comes with losing a left tackle, is this leaves Jacksonville paper-thin at tackle.

text:
Trevor Lawrence's blind side protector, Anton Harrison, is done for the rest of the season due to a torn ACL. Harrison underwent arthroscopic surgery on Thursday, but during the surgery, doctors discovered he had torn his ACL as well, according to ESPN.

Harrison, 24, hurt his knee in Week 5 during Jacksonville's eventual win over the Eagles in London and was carted off. The Jaguars, who also played in London in Week 6, placed Harrison on IR but were hopeful he'd be able to return at some point this season. Then Thursday's surgery revealed the full scope of the injury.

The No. 27 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, Harrison moved from right tackle to left tackle this offseason. It had been a bit of an up-and-down year for him in his new spot -- he allowed three sacks and 12 pressures in just five games -- but it's a significant loss for Jacksonville nonetheless.

Veteran swing Walker Little took over for Harrison in Week 5 and started in his stead in Week 6 against the Texans. The good news for Jacksonville is that Little has significant experience (40 career starts) and performed ably -- no sacks, two pressures allowed -- in Week 6 against a ferocious Houston front.

The bad news, outside the obvious bad news that comes with losing a left tackle, is this leaves Jacksonville paper-thin at tackle. Little was the only tackle on the roster outside Harrison and starting right tackle Cole Van Lanen. The Jaguars do have veteran offensive lineman Geron Christian Sr. on the practice squad but could look to make moves ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

Jaguars options

Roll with Walker Little

A second-round pick out of Stanford in 2021, Little has spent his entire career with the Jaguars, and he started at least three games every year from 2021-25. Last year, he started 14 games, including 12 at left tackle. Overall, he allowed 2.9 pressures per game, the second-highest rate among offensive linemen, only behind Tennessee's Dan Moore Jr., and nine sacks, tied for third-most. He also committed seven penalties. By the end of the season, the Jaguars had moved him to right guard and moved Van Lanen to left tackle.

But coach Liam Coen said last week, "I have a lot of confidence" in Little.

"I probably can't overstate how important it is because we really are fortunate to not have to play a backup in a situation when a tackle goes down," Coen said a day later. "I don't look at Walker as a backup tackle or a backup guard."

This -- plus calling up someone from the practice squad -- seems to be the clear solution for now, but if Little struggles, the Jaguars could pursue other options.

Move Cole Van Lanen to left tackle

Van Lanen impressed moving over to left tackle late last season, so much so that he got a three-year, $51 million extension. Should Coen and his staff deem it worth doing again, they already have proof of concept.

The issue, though, is that it would create a hole at right tackle, where Van Lanen has worked the past several months. Little stepped in for some snaps at right tackle in two games this season, but both times were at the end of blowouts. He has never played meaningful right tackle snaps in his NFL career, though the Jaguars clearly trusted him to do so, considering he was their swing tackle prior to Harrison's injury.

Trade for Fred Johnson or Andrew Wylie

Unfortunately for Jacksonville, it's not like capable left tackles are a dime a dozen. However, there are some options potentially available before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

The Commanders and the Eagles are two potential sellers in the lowly NFC East. The Eagles have already traded away Cam Jurgens amid a nightmarish season for the entire organization. Last year, the Jaguars traded Fred Johnson to Philadelphia for a 2026 seventh-round pick. Might they be interested in a reunion?

Andrew Wylie is another name that could be of interest. He has not played meaningful snaps at left tackle, but he has played a ton at right tackle, right guard and left guard. If anything, he could be the Jaguars' swing tackle, the role Little had before Harrison's injury. Wylie has played sparingly this season, though it was at left tackle.

text:
As if things couldn’t get any worse for the Los Angeles Rams, they could now be without another star playmaker.

Star wide receiver Puka Nacua left Rams practice early on Thursday due to a calf injury, putting his status for Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders into question. Nacua was later listed as limited on the Rams' injury report.

The Rams' offense is already without wide receiver Davante Adams, who was placed on injured reserve with a ruptured hamstring. With Adams sidelined for six to 10 weeks and Nacua now dealing with a calf injury, the injury list for Los Angeles continues to grow.

Nacua’s season has been plagued by injury trouble, as he already missed two games earlier this year with a hip issue.

When healthy, however, Nacua has been highly productive. He has hauled in 37 receptions for 417 yards and a touchdown across four games, highlighted by a showing against the Buffalo Bills where he caught a career-high 17 passes for 138 yards and a touchdown.

After entering the season as Super Bowl favorites due to their blockbuster offseason, it’s been a downward spiral for the Rams. Star edge rusher Myles Garrett hasn't played since Week 1 due to a knee injury that required surgery.

He is on IR with a hamstring injury.

He would be a backup and special teams guy, if healthy.

text:
The San Francisco 49ers are thriving at 6-0 entering Sunday's showdown against the Atlanta Falcons.

They're coming off a 23-17 victory over the Washington Commanders on Monday night and are now one of three remaining unbeaten teams in the NFL.

However, San Francisco is still navigating the injury bug. Veteran wide receiver Mike Evans' status for Week 7 is in doubt after he left Monday's game with an Achilles issue he was already dealing with before kickoff.

49ers GM Announces Update on Evans

Although the injury doesn't appear serious, 49ers general manager John Lynch discussed Evans' status during his weekly appearance on KNBR.

Lynch said Evans' status remains undetermined and noted that he "wouldn't say it's not likely" that the wide receiver suits up Sunday.

"I wouldn't say not likely, I think it's still TBD," Lynch said. "We've got a couple more days, we're going to take every bit of those. He's done a really good job treating this thing and we know of Mike's toughness… He's that type of player that you wait and let it play itself out."

The 49ers have a bye next week, so Evans could get two weeks of rest if the team chooses to sit him. Lynch was asked about that possibility Thursday, as fans have urged San Francisco to rest the veteran wide receiver while the team remains 6-0.

"I absolutely love our fans… There's gonna be noise, our job is not to focus on the noise but to focus on what we believe is right for our football team and that's what we continue to do," Lynch added.

Evans' Practice Status

Now in his 13th NFL season, Evans has become such a veteran that he doesn't necessarily need extensive practice time to suit up for a game.

He showed that last week when he barely practiced while managing his ongoing rib injury and Achilles soreness. However, he played Monday night and recorded three receptions for 94 yards before exiting in the second quarter.

CHICAGO -- Bears tight end Cole Kmet exited Chicago's 30-24 win over the New England Patriots on Thursday night on a cart because of an injury to his right knee.

With 5:46 to play in the fourth quarter, Kmet caught an 8-yard pass from Caleb Williams and took a hard hit while running up the Bears' sideline. The tight end collided with Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez and linebacker Robert Spillane, and immediately grabbed for his knee while on the ground.

Kmet got to his feet with the help of trainers but could not put weight on his right leg. He gave the crowd at Soldier Field a thumbs-up as he was carted back to the locker room, where he was quickly ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Coach Ben Johnson said the Bears will find out more about the severity of Kmet's injury on Friday.

"I don't think it looked very good," Johnson said.

Williams had a similar response after watching Kmet leave the game with what appeared to be a serious injury.

"It was tough," Williams said. "I don't know exactly what it is and all of that, but obviously being carted off is never good. You're at least going to miss some time. And so he's been through it, and it's challenging, it's tough and I'll be with him. I'll be right there with him through every step of whatever the injury is. And Cole's been there for me every step of the way through the first year, the second year and now through this year. I could only do the same for him."

text:
The Seahawks announced a couple of roster transactions ahead of their Week 7 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. The happy and expected news was Zach Charbonnet being activated from the PUP list. The bad news is Elijah Arroyo has been placed on injured reserve. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Thursday that Arroyo will have to undergo shoulder surgery and will miss the rest of the 2026 NFL season.

Arroyo injured his shoulder last week against the Denver Broncos while attempting to recover Rashid Shaheed’s fumble. Coming out of the Broncos game, it did not sound positive. In fact, an injured reserve stint was expected for Arroyo. That his season is already over is surely a big blow for the second-year tight end out of Miami.

Arroyo had an electric 2026 training camp, which brought a lot of optimism that Arroyo could have a big sophomore jump this season. Unfortunately this strong training camp did not continue into the regular season. Arroyo has seldom seen any targets this season and will finish his 2026 season with only one catch for 17 yards and 0 touchdowns.

Entering the draft, Arroyo was heralded for his pass catching ability. However, with questions around his blocking ability and injury history (including an ACL tear), Arroyo managed to slip to Seattle at 50th overall. Unfortunately, the injury concerns have continued for Arroyo into the NFL. Arroyo missed the back-end of the 2025 regular season after injuring his knee in Week 14.

As for the Seahawks, their tight end room is left with AJ Barner, Eric Saubert, and Nick Kallerup on the 53-man roster, with Josiah Deguara recently joining the practice squad. Saubert and Kallerup are known for their blocking rather than receiving abilities. Because of this, Seattle could potentially add a bigger pass catcher to the active roster.

text:
RENTON, Wash. -- The Seattle Seahawks activated running back Zach Charbonnet off the physically unable to perform list Thursday, an expected move amid his comeback from a torn ACL.

It's not certain that Charbonnet, who is only eight months removed from surgery, will make his season debut Sunday night when the Seahawks host the Kansas City Chiefs at Lumen Field. Coach Mike Macdonald said earlier this week that it's a "possibility" that he plays "in some capacity."

The Seahawks listed Charbonnet as a full participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday.

"Just taking it a day at a time," Charbonnet said Thursday in his first comments to reporters since he was injured in January. "But whenever I'm out there, it's going to be special and I'm just going to be happy to get back out there."

The Seahawks on Thursday also placed second-year tight end Elijah Arroyo on injured reserve. A source told ESPN's Adam Schefter that Arroyo, a 2025 second-round pick who caught one pass for 17 yards in six games this season, is having season-ending surgery to repair a shoulder injury he suffered last week in a loss to the Denver Broncos.

Charbonnet had been listed as limited on the first eight injury reports released by the team since it designated him to return to practice Oct. 1. Thursday marked the 21-day deadline to move Charbonnet to the 53-man roster.

In a co-starting role last season alongside Kenneth Walker III, Charbonnet rushed for 730 yards and a team-high 12 touchdowns. He tore his left ACL in Seattle's divisional round win over the San Francisco 49ers on Jan. 17 and had surgery Feb. 12.

Charbonnet said this was "around" the time that he was aiming to return.

"I'm feeling pretty good," Charbonnet said. "Just going a day at a time. Seeing how it adapts with picking up practice and stuff like that."

With Charbonnet beginning the season on PUP and rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price missing the last three games with a chest injury, Seattle is averaging 107.2 rushing yards per game and 3.9 yards per carry, both of which rank 18th. Their backfield trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani have combined to lose four fumbles.

Price, who was placed on IR in Week 4, has to miss at least one more game.

text:
LOS ANGELES -- Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua left Thursday's practice with a calf injury, a team spokesperson said.

Nacua was listed on the injury report as a limited participant in Thursday's practice.

The Rams were already without wide receiver Davante Adams, who injured his hamstring in their Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals. Adams will miss six to 10 weeks with the injury, coach Sean McVay said Monday.

Nacua missed the Rams' Week 2 and 3 games with a psoas injury. In four games this season, Nacua has 37 catches for 417 yards and a touchdown.

Nacua is the latest in a long list of injury updates this week. Along with Adams, the Rams are without nose tackle Poona Ford, who will miss the rest of the season with a ruptured triceps, and defensive tackle Kobie Turner, who will miss "a handful of weeks" with a groin injury. The Rams also lost kicker Blake Grupe to a torn ACL in Week 6.

text:
After already losing several starters to injured reserve this week, the Los Angeles Rams took another hit on offense Thursday. According to reporters, Puka Nacua left practice early after suffering a calf injury. He was officially a limited participant in practice, though the severity of the injury is not yet known.

Sean McVay will address the media on Friday, at which point he will provide an update on the Rams' star receiver.

Nacua dealt with a hip/groin injury earlier this season, missing two games in Weeks 2 and 3. He returned in Week 4 and picked up right where he left off with back-to-back 100-yard games against the Eagles and Bills.

The Rams are set to take on the Raiders this Sunday in a pivotal Week 7 game. Davante Adams is already on IR with a ruptured hamstring, so Los Angeles can't afford to lose Nacua, too.

After practice on Friday, the Rams will release their final injury report with game statuses for Nacua and any other players who are banged up.

Bengals vs. Ravens Injury Report
text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are looking good on the injury front as they prepare for a big AFC North clash with the Baltimore Ravens. On the other side, Baltimore may have a chance to get their franchise quarterback back on the field, according to Thursday's reporting.

For the Bengals, safety Kyle Dugger (quad) was upgraded to a full participant on Thursday. It is unknown whether he will play on Sunday, but he appears to be trending toward a return after being out since Week 3.

Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen and B.J. Hill both got a veteran's rest day.

For Baltimore, quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle) was listed as a limited participant Thursday. On Wednesday, he was listed as limited as well, but it sounds like he got a decent amount more work done in Thursday's practice.

Media members reported Jackson was active in practice and wasn't seen favoring the ankle that has kept him out of the lineup since October 4th. Media wasn't present for the entire practice, so that reporting is essentially just from warmups.

Baltimore's new center Cam Jergens (concussion) was a full participant for the second day in a row. If he clears the NFL's concussion protocol, he should make his Ravens debut on Sunday.

Safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) was downgraded to a nonparticipant after being limited on Wednesday, so his availability for Sunday is in question.

Linebacker Tavius Robinson (pectoral) was also out.

text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. (KCTV) - Kansas City Chiefs left tackle Josh Simmons is being placed on injured reserve due to a back injury that has sidelined him for more than two months.

On Thursday, Chiefs Vice President of Sports Medicine and Performance Rick Burkholder shared details of Simmons’ injury timeline and next steps with the media.

Burkholder said Simmons -- who has dealt with a bulging disc in his lower back since training camp -- will go on injured reserve after practicing in a limited capacity last week.

Burkholder said the Chiefs, Simmons and his representation decided the 2025 first-round pick should go on injured reserve because they determined he had stalled in his rehab process.

“We feel that he’s plateaued in the rehab process, as he’s trying to get to the final steps of recovery with return to competition,” Burkholder said. “And he’s just not there yet.”

Burkholder said Simmons came to him on Aug. 17 following a training camp practice in which he felt trouble in his calf area on the same leg he tore his patellar tendon in college. An MRI conducted in St. Joseph, Missouri, determined Simmons had a bulging, herniated disc in his lumbar spine. Burkholder said the disc problem was higher up than the team typically sees in offensive linemen, “which complicated the case.”

A second opinion with a spine specialist in California determined rehab, rather than surgery, was recommended.

“A few weeks later,” Burkholder said, “the repeat MRI a few weeks later showed that the disc had improved, so no surgery was recommended and rehab would continue.”

Burkholder said Simmons’ rehab was diligent, but the lack of progress has now resulted in the team making a move.

“Josh worked his tail off,” Burkholder said. “He worked diligently with my staff every day and has improved to the point where he returned to practice in a limited capacity last week.”

Simmons was listed as a non-participant in Wednesday’s practice as the Chiefs prepare for a ‘Sunday Night Football’ matchup with the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. The Chiefs listed Simmons’ absence as due to “back/personal,” which Burkholder said was to give Simmons “some time to talk with his family and his representatives to investigate next steps as he goes through this process.”

That process led to the decision to place Simmons on injured reserve, though Simmons still does not need surgery.

“He’ll continue with the rehab process with the goal of returning to play at a high level that he achieved in the past,” Burkholder said. “I just give (Simmons) a ton of credit for navigating through this injury to the point where surgery is not recommended and that he needs more time to return to full function.”

Now, Simmons will not be eligible to return for at least four games, meaning the Ohio State product who has missed 14 of a possible 22 games during his career will not be allowed to play until at least a Week 11 matchup with the Arizona Cardinals.

Without Simmons, undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson has started at left tackle in each of Kansas City’s first five games.

title: 49ers are to Blame for Mike Evans' Achilles Injury - Sports Illustrated
description:
He left Monday night’s game against the Commanders right before halftime with an Achilles injury and wouldn’t return.
Anytime a player leaves a game with an Achilles injury, it causes panic.
Evans’ injury is twofold.
The 49ers deserve blame for Evans’ Achilles injury.
Evans didn’t take part in a single practice in the lead-up to Monday night against the Commanders because of Achilles soreness.
text:
Mike Evans was expectedly held out of the 49ers’ first Week 7 practice against the Falcons.

He left Monday night’s game against the Commanders right before halftime with an Achilles injury and wouldn’t return. Anytime a player leaves a game with an Achilles injury, it causes panic.

Thankfully, Evans didn’t suffer a season-ending Achilles tear. But he is experiencing tendinitis. It would be very surprising if Evans plays this week against the Falcons, especially with the Bye week after.

Evans’ injury is twofold. On one hand, it’s a sigh of relief that Evans didn’t tear his Achilles. On the other hand, he shouldn’t have gotten hurt against the Commanders because he shouldn’t have played.

The 49ers deserve blame for Evans’ Achilles injury. Evans didn’t take part in a single practice in the lead-up to Monday night against the Commanders because of Achilles soreness.

That should’ve been a red flag to the 49ers. They, of all teams, should know how serious Achilles injuries are, even if it’s just soreness. It happened two years ago with Christian McCaffrey.

You’d think they’d learn that it’s best to be extremely cautious with a player who’s dealing with any Achilles-related issue. Instead, they allowed Evans to play because he wanted to. They failed to protect him from himself.

“Mike's got a lot of experience doing this stuff,” Kyle Shanahan said in Monday night’s postgame. “Mike's pretty honest with us too, and my life experiences with him over six games, if he says he's ready to go, I believe him.”

Believing in Evans is foolish. What NFL star doesn’t want to play, no matter how they’re feeling? Evans isn’t thinking about the consequences and risks of playing through Achilles soreness.

All that matters to him is playing and helping his team. That’s how tough he is, but he doesn’t need to prove anything to anyone. What he needs is someone to hold him out from worsening his injury.

The 49ers failed to prevent that because Evans wanted to play. They let him play that game as if it were against the Seahawks in December, with the NFC West on the line.

Now, they have to rely on Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing, and a newly signed Brandin Cooks. The wide receiver position was already razor-thin.

It's desolate now, and it opens the floodgates for 49ers fans to pound the table for a wide receiver trade. This all could've been avoided if they had sat him against the Commanders.

What a blunder.

text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- The Kansas City Chiefs placed left tackle Josh Simmons on injured reserve Thursday, further delaying his return from a bulging, herniated disk in his lower back.

After being a limited participant in the Chiefs' three practices last week, Simmons still felt pain in his back and left leg, the same leg he had previously suffered a torn patellar tendon in back in October 2024 while playing for Ohio State.

Head trainer Rick Burkholder shared Thursday that Simmons reported feeling discomfort in his left calf following a training camp practice Aug. 17, prompting the team to order an MRI, which revealed a "bulging, herniated" disk, he said.

"That disk problem was higher up than what we normally see in most of our offensive linemen, which complicated the case," Burkholder said of Simmons. "The repeat MRI, a few weeks later, showed that the disk had improved, so no surgery was recommended. Josh worked his tail off. He worked diligently with my staff every day. However, we feel he has plateaued in the rehab process. He's just not there yet."

Burkholder then explained that Simmons took the rest of Wednesday afternoon off to discuss the next steps of his treatment with his family and his representative, thus the "personal" and "back" designations on the Chiefs' injury report.

According to Burkholder, "everybody" agreed that Simmons needed to be placed on injured reserve, a move that will force the lineman to miss at least the next four games -- against Seattle, Denver, the New York Jets and Atlanta. The earliest Simmons can return is Week 11, when the Chiefs host the Arizona Cardinals on Nov. 22.

The team and Simmons are still determining how and where he will continue his rehab.

"I give a lot of credit to Josh, my physicians and my staff for navigating through this injury to the point where surgery is not recommended," Burkholder added. "He just needs more time to return to full function."

Simmons' absence has opened the door for undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson, who played right tackle in college for the Indiana Hoosiers. Benson is the first undrafted offensive rookie to start in Week 1 for Andy Reid during his entire 14-year coaching tenure in Kansas City. Benson has done a commendable job as the lineman most responsible for protecting the blind side of quarterback Patrick Mahomes, earning NFL Offensive Rookie of the Month in September.

On the other side, right tackle Jaylon Moore, a five-year veteran, is currently in the NFL's concussion protocol. Joshua Ezeudu, who joined the Chiefs in late August via a trade with the New York Giants, is expected to start in Moore's place in Sunday night's road game against the Seahawks.

Since selecting Simmons in the first round of the 2025 NFL draft, the Chiefs have played more games without him (14) than with him (eight). The last time Simmons played was last year on Thanksgiving Day, when the team fell to the Dallas Cowboys. During that game, Simmons suffered a dislocated and fractured left wrist, a season-ending injury that required surgery. Before that setback, Simmons was an emerging rookie, as he allowed a pressure rate of just 6.6%, which at the time was the third-lowest mark among left tackles and the second lowest by a rookie left tackle since 2018 (minimum 150 pass blocks), according to Next Gen Stats.

"His job is to make sure that he's physically getting himself ready for what's next," offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy said Thursday of Simmons "He's just got to focus one day at a time."

text:
No. 26 is back.

Philadelphia Eagles star running back Saquon Barkley is expected to return to practice Thursday and play in the team's Monday night matchup at home against the Dallas Cowboys, NFL Media reported on Thursday morning.

Barkley missed Philadelphia's last two games due to a hamstring injury that he suffered in the team's Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.

The Eagles have also been without running backs Tank Bigbsy (placed on injured reserve on Oct. 6 due to core muscle surgery) and Will Shipley (placed on injured reserve on Oct. 16 due to a foot injury).

With Barkley sidelined, Dameon Pierce rushed for 49 yards and one score on 2.1 yards per carry over the Eagles' last two games. Philadelphia also has running back Elijah Mitchell on its practice squad.

Prior to the injury, Barkley, the 2024 NFL Offensive Player of the Year Award winner, rushed for 182 yards and zero touchdowns on 5.1 yards per carry.

In all, the Eagles' offense is just 29th in the NFL in rushing yards (82.2 per game), 24th in total yards (311.2 per game), 23rd in passing yards (194.3 per game) and 19th in points (22.3 per game).

Barkley is coming off an underwhelming season by his standards, as the three-time Pro Bowler rushed for 1,140 yards and seven touchdowns on 4.1 yards per carry in 2025. This was after Barkley became just the ninth player in NFL history to rush for 2,000 yards in a single season in 2024, tallying 2,005 yards and 13 rushing scores on 5.8 yards carry en route to Philadelphia winning Super Bowl LIX.

Barkley's return comes in the wake of the Eagles placing quarterback Jalen Hurts on injured reserve and his season over due to blood clots in both the quarterback's calf and lungs.

Tanner McKee, who started in the team's Week 6 loss to the Carolina Panthers, is expected to be under center for the Eagles moving forward.

With quarterback Jalen Hurts likely to miss the remainder of the season, the offense needs to have a steady presence on the ground.

Starting in place of Hurts, Tanner McKee went 26-of-45 for 215 yards and a touchdown in Week 6. As backup quarterbacks go, Philadelphia could probably do worse, but there's a massive gulf in quality between Hurts and McKee.

Having Barkley in the backfield will take some pressure off McKee.

Whether he's enough to meaningfully alter the trajectory of the Eagles' season is another question. They're 2-4 and in the midst of a four-game losing streak. No team has been more snakebitten in terms of injuries.

The franchise will want to avoid a rebuild at all costs, but one or two more losses will make a playoff push extremely difficult.

Nix said he's not playing scared and he's not worried about getting hurt, but he acknowledged the mental part of returning from an injury.

text:
This season, Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix hasn't looked like the 2024-2025 quarterback who frequently used his legs to extend plays and fight for extra yards.

Nix has seemingly turned down opportunities to run this fall, and he's avoided hits that he took on in his first two seasons, leading some fans and pundits to speculate that the QB still has last season's ankle injury on the back of his mind. Nix was asked about the mental aspect of returning from an injury following Wednesday's practice, and the third-year QB admitted that it plays a role in each player's recovery.

"You know, I'd be lying if I said no," Nix said. "I think that's just what happens. I think you come back and you're like, you know, every day is a progression. It's like you're doing treatment for the whole entire year. And I'm not necessarily doing physical therapy treatment, but I'm out there on the practice field getting rep after rep, trying to get back in super great shape so my carries can go up, so I'm ready when my number's called and when I can run. But I'm not scared; I'm not physically, like, worried. I just think there's something to the sport.

"I think all guys, when they come back from an injury, it's just like doing it one day at a time. I think that's just part of the game, part of the process. You know, I had surgery, probably, I think, six months ago, you know? It takes a while for things to fully re-engage and re-come back, and I'm confident in myself. I know I'm going to get back and be exactly what I was, if not better, because as I get older, that's how it's been. But I do think it's just one game at a time, and my training is going like this (gestures up), and at the end of the day, it's all about getting better."

Nix said he's not playing scared and he's not worried about getting hurt, but he acknowledged the mental part of returning from an injury. He later reiterated that he feels great, and his speed numbers have increased in training.

After another week of reps in practice this week, Nix will look to take the next step when the Broncos go on the road to face the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7.

text:
HOUSTON (AP) — Tank Dell will play his first game in nearly two years on Sunday, and the Houston Texans are thrilled that their receiver is back after a catastrophic knee injury.

Coach DeMeco Ryans said Wednesday that they aren’t putting any expectations on Dell’s performance against the New York Giants after he was out for so long and that it will just be exciting to see him back on the field.

“The main thing is him just going out playing ball,” Ryans said. “I don’t care how many reps he gets, but I’ll have my Tank Dell jersey on on Sunday.”

Defensive end Will Anderson Jr. shared that enthusiasm when discussing Dell’s return.

“I’ve been hugging Tank all day,” Anderson said. “I haven’t left his side all day. ... I was telling him, every time I saw him today, I said, ‘Bro, I’m so proud of you, man.’”

Dell missed all last season and the first six games this season recovering from a dislocated knee and multiple torn knee ligaments he sustained on Dec. 21, 2024. He had 51 receptions for 667 yards and three scores before his injury in what was his second NFL season.

He has a lot of emotions as his return approaches after many long and tough months filled with hard work and rehabilitation.

“I’m anxious, of course. It’s been two years, well (almost) two years, since I’ve played,” he said. “But I don’t think I’m overwhelmed. I’m anxious to get back out there and play some football. I’m blessed, man.”

And he’s envisioned what it will be like when he makes that long-awaited first grab.

“I don’t care if the first catch is 2 yards. I’m spiking the ball,” he said half-jokingly. “And it’s going to feel good. I know there’s a lot of questions like how’s he going to look when he gets tackled? I don’t care about none of that. I’m ready to get tackled. ... Y’all are going to see the passion I have after I have that first catch.”

His most recent injury wasn’t the only one Dell has dealt with since the Texans drafted him in the third round in 2023 following a standout career at the University of Houston. His rookie season, where he scored seven touchdowns, was cut short when he broke his leg in Week 13.

Quarterback C.J. Stroud, who counts Dell among his closest friends, saw everything he did behind the scenes to get to this point and raved about how he approached the entire process.

“The main thing is he always had a smile on his face, even probably when he wasn’t feeling like smiling,” Stroud said. “His attitude through the whole process has been great.”

Dell returns to a crowded receiver room that recently added star Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with Arizona. He isn’t worried about getting his touches and is simply excited to contribute to the talented group.

While Dell can’t wait to play on Sunday, there is one drawback to his return. So many people want to come to the game to support him that it’s costing him a pretty penny.

“I had to buy so many extra tickets. I’m kinda upset about that,” he said with a laugh. “But I’m happy because they were with me through this whole journey.”

A very special guest will be his grandmother, whom he paid to fly from Florida to be at Reliant Stadium on Sunday.

After playing collegiately in town and making so many electric plays in his first two seasons with the team, Dell is undoubtedly a favorite among Texans fans.

And he can’t wait to see how they respond to him on Sunday.

“I feel like they’re going to go crazy,” he said. “I’m excited for that.”

text:
The Cleveland Browns opened practice on Wednesday with their full projected running back depth chart for the first time since the season opener.

Per Daniel Oyefusi, Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson suited up for the team’s first on-field day of prep for Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans. Judkins and Sampson both missed practice time last week and were ultimately ruled out for Sunday’s win over the Baltimore Ravens.

Head coach Todd Monken told reporters that he's optimistic both will be available for this week's trip to Tennessee.

It’s a positive development for a Browns team that’s been searching for consistency on offense.

Even better? The team appears to be getting healthier at the perfect time.

The Browns are finally getting healthier at the perfect time

Mason Graham appears poised for a full week of participation

Graham was back on the practice field Wednesday, which is a great sign for his availability against the Titans. He missed both the Jets and Ravens games after suffering a sprained MCL during Cleveland’s prime-time victory over the Steelers on Oct. 1.

Monken said Graham was pushing to play against the Ravens.

The Browns decided to give Graham an extra week of rest after he practiced in a limited capacity last Friday. Barring a setback, he should be a full-go against a Titans offense that ranks dead-last in scoring at 14 points per game.

Grant Delpit sits out while working through the NFL’s concussion protocol

Delpit exited the Ravens game in the first half with a concussion. He wasn’t cleared to return to the field on Wednesday, which puts his Week 7 status in some doubt.

The final two phases of the league’s five-step protocol require non-contact training drills (or what would be referred to as limited practice participation on the injury report) before a player is cleared for unrestricted practice and contact. Delpit, who is also managing a shoulder injury, could have a tough time returning this week if he’s not able to get in a limited session on Thursday, though that’s not necessarily a must.

It’s worth noting that wide receiver KC Concepcion practiced in full last Wednesday after progressing rather quickly through concussion protocol following the Jets game. Each player’s situation is different, and Delpit’s practice participation going forward will be the best gauge for his availability.

Rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren and veteran Daniel Thomas both saw added playing time in Delpit’s absence last week.

Browns continue to manage Carson Schwesinger’s practice reps

Schwesinger spent the majority of last week in a walking boot, but he didn’t appear to be limited by his sprained ankle. He played every defensive snap, led the team in tackles, and forced a game-swinging fumble on Derrick Henry in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s big win.

Cleveland’s star middle linebacker was a nonparticipant in practice to open the week, but this is Carson Schwesinger we’re talking about. His leg remains attached, so fans should expect him to be on the field as usual in Week 7.

Defensive linemen Mike Hall Jr., Kalia Davis remain iffy to start the week

Hall hasn’t logged a practice since the Steelers game as he continues to rehab an ankle injury. He remained off the practice field on Wednesday.

Davis, who’s been out since the start of training camp with a quad issue, has been operating within a 21-day practice window that’s set to expire next week. It’s unclear if Davis experienced a setback, but he logged one limited practice session ahead of Week 5 and hasn’t suited up since.

Veteran offensive linemen Elgton Jenkins (knee) and Teven Jenkins (back) were both held out of Wednesday’s practice as well. Elgton Jenkins played all 68 offensive snaps in the Ravens game last week. Teven Jenkins hasn’t appeared in a game this season after injuring his back in a practice ahead of Week 1.

text:
It’s Drake Maye versus Caleb Williams as the New England Patriots visit the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field Thursday night.

Going into Thursday's matchup, both teams are 4-2. And it's a short week for the Bears, who beat the Falcons Sunday afternoon 31 to 23.

It's also a short week for Williams, who missed three games after a hamstring injury before returning Sunday in Atlanta. He showed no signs of any rust, going 30 for 36 for 305 yards and a touchdown in the Bears' victory over the Falcons.

Maye has completed 64.1% of his passes for 878 yards and 10 touchdowns during New England’s three-game winning streak, throwing just one interception during the impressive stretch.

Williams, 24, was No. 1 pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. Maye, also 24, was No. 3.

As the game approaches, here's what to know.

Bears injury report

Local

The Chicago Bears’ final injury report features bad news about running back Kyle Monangai, who was ruled out for a third consecutive week as he continues to deal with thumb and toe injuries.

They will also be without linebacker Jack Sanborn, who remains in the NFL’s concussion protocol.

As for linebacker TJ Edwards, the Bears have classified him as doubtful for Thursday’s game, but he was upgraded to a “limited” participant in Wednesday’s walkthrough at Halas Hall.

Defensive back Tyrique Stevenson was classified as a full participant throughout the week in practice, but is listed as questionable for Thursday’s game.

Finally, linebacker Keyshaun Elliott and offensive guard Jonah Jackson are both expected to play, as they were not given injury designations for the contest.

On the Patriots’ side of things, they will be without both of their starting offensive guards, as Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown were both ruled out for Thursday’s game.

Starting cornerback Carlton Davis III will also be ruled out for Thursday with a neck injury, and reserve corners Channing Canada and Karon Prunty will both miss the game with hamstring injuries.

Former Bears safety Kevin Byard III is questionable to play with a chest injury, as is starting linebacker Christian Elliss, according to the Patriots.

Their offensive line may take another hit depending on the health of starting right tackle Morgan Moses, who is questionable to play with a foot injury. Starting strong safety Craig Woodson is also questionable with a shoulder injury.

Bears game time and channel: How to watch

Kick-off for Thursday Night Football is set for 7:15 p.m. at Soldier Field.

According to the NFL, the game will air on Prime Video. For Bears fans in the Chicago area, the game will also be available locally on Fox, according to the NFL.

Mike Ditka tribute

The matchup marks the Bears' first home game since the passing of legendary coach Mike Ditka.

In addition to the No. 89 patches the team will wear on its jerseys for the remainder of the season, the Bears will also honor Ditka with a pregame moment of silence prior to Thursday’s contest against the New England Patriots, and they will also unveil an on-field stencil dedicated to the former tight end and coach.

The team’s “spirit squad” will also wave Ditka-inspired flags during the pregame ceremonies according to the Bears.

As for fans, there will be plenty of opportunities to honor Ditka. According to the Bears, every fan in attendance at Thursday’s game will receive a Ditka mustache to wear during the game. The first 10,000 fans will also receive a Bears knit headband, inspired by Ditka’s signature sweater that he wore during numerous big moments for the team.

Appropriately enough, these tributes are all taking place as the Bears take on the Patriots, the team Ditka and the Monsters of the Midway defeated for their Super Bowl championship in New Orleans in 1986.

Lamar Jackson is finally back on the practice field in some capacity.

Coach Jesse Minter said the quarterback got "limited work in" during practice on Wednesday, though he called Jackson’s recovery "a day-by-day thing."

Jackson has missed the last two games since spraining his left ankle in an Oct. 4 win over the Titans.

Tyler Huntley led a comeback win in Atlanta in Week 5, before Baltimore fell 13-10 to the Browns last Sunday. At 4-2, the Ravens host the division-rival Bengals this week in a pivotal AFC North matchup.

Minter had said Monday that Jackson could "potentially" practice this week, and Wednesday’s work is the first sign his return to the lineup could be close.

The Patriots and Bears both have injury concerns heading into Thursday night’s game at Soldier Field.

Chicago ruled out running back Kyle Monangai, who will miss his third straight game with a thumb injury and turf toe. Linebacker Jack Sanborn is also out with a concussion.

New England ruled out five players: guards Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Ben Brown (knee), and cornerbacks Carlton Davis III (neck), Karon Prunty (hamstring) and Channing Canada (hamstring).

The Patriots will have receiver A.J. Brown, who is off the injury report. Davis will miss his third straight game, and the Patriots haven’t had him and Christian Gonzalez on the field together since Week 3.

text:
There was some good news from the Miami Dolphins' first injury report off their bye involving rookie draft picks Caleb Douglas and Kyle Louis, but it did come with a caveat.

Both players were listed as limited participants, and there's absolutely no guarantee that either will be ready to go for the Week 7 game against the New York Jets.

Douglas was non-committal about his availability when he spoke to reporters after practice Wednesday, and head coach Jeff Hafley also didn't make any promises beforehand.

"He was a big bright spot early on," Hafley said. "Everybody was excited about him from training camp to preseason and the first couple games that he played. We were counting on him and then unfortunately he got injured. Monday he was out there, limited. Today he'll be out there and getting acclimated again. My expectations can't be too high because we've got to see him practice today. We've got to see how he feels tomorrow, kind of like Kyle. And then Friday to see what he's able to do and if he's able to go and help us out. But I am excited. I'm very excited. We've got two young players practicing that we're excited about, and we'll see what they can do today."

The bottom line here is that having Douglas and Louis back will help when they're able to return, but maybe it won't happen this week, and if it does, maybe we shouldn't expect too much too soon from either of them.

Douglas hasn't played since Week 2, while Louis has been out since sustaining a knee injury in the opener against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Also back at practice Wednesday was edge defender Robert Beal Jr., who missed the past three games because of a hamstring injury. He also was listed as a limited participant in practice.

THE DOLPHINS INJURY OUTLOOK

Cornerback Reese Taylor, who continues to deal with a quad injury, was the only player on the 53-man roster who did not practice Wednesday.

Along with Beal, Douglas and Louis, long-snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), tight end Will Kacmarek (hamstring) and running back Jaylen Wright (foot) all were listed as limited participants.

The Dolphins had four starter listed as full participants, including quarterback Malik Willis, who is dealing with an issue with his right thumb. Willis appeared to hit his throwing hand on a helmet during the Week 5 game against the Cincinnati Bengals.

LB Jordyn Brooks (foot), G Jonah Savaiinaea (ankle) and CB JuJu Brents (heel) also were listed as full participants, as was linebacker Jackson Woodard (ankle).

For the Jets, the most significant news was running back Breece Hall not practicing because of a quad injury. He has missed the past three games.

title: Vikings praise Aaron Jones Sr.'s heart with Jordan Mason out - ESPN
authors: Kevin Seifert, Mel Kiper Jr, Jordan Reid, Anthony Gharib, Jenna Laine, NFL Nation, Bill Barnwell, Chris Wright, Nick Wagoner, ESPN staff
description:

The Vikings entered the season planning to rotate Jones and Mason as part of a revitalized running game.
Had the injury occurred later in the season, the Vikings might have felt more comfortable moving Claiborne or Dallas into the rotation.

text:
EAGAN, Minn. -- The Minnesota Vikings should return to full strength at running back Sunday, when veteran Jordan Mason is expected to return from a fractured finger against the Indianapolis Colts (1 pm. ET, CBS). So now is the perfect time to understand and recognize what Aaron Jones Sr. achieved during Mason's four-game absence.

Jones, who turns 32 in December, pushed through perhaps the most grueling month of his 10-year career to play a key role in the Vikings' 5-0 start.

With rookie Demond Claiborne not yet ready for regular work, and veteran newcomer DeeJay Dallas earmarked mostly for special teams, Jones took 90% of the Vikings' running back carries and played 81% of the team's overall offensive snaps.

His 85 carries and 97 total touches were second most in the NFL over that period, and they were by far the most he has accumulated in a four-game stretch during a single season of his career, according to ESPN Research. And Jones did most of it with a sprained MCL in his left knee, an injury he said he has suffered on two other occasions in previous seasons but had never been able to play through.

During a conversation Wednesday with ESPN, Jones acknowledged his pride in answering the call under unique circumstances.

"They can measure your height," he said. "They can measure your weight. They can't measure your heart. That's something my dad taught me."

The Vikings entered the season planning to rotate Jones and Mason as part of a revitalized running game. Mason took 15 carries and played 48% of the snaps in the Vikings' Week 1 victory over the Green Bay Packers, while Jones took 12 and played 43% of the snaps.

But Mason reported soreness the next day and soon had surgery. Had the injury occurred later in the season, the Vikings might have felt more comfortable moving Claiborne or Dallas into the rotation. But for Weeks 2-5, Jones was the only back coach Kevin O'Connell wanted to use.

Jones, however, didn't make it very far before encountering his own adversity, suffering the MCL injury in Week 2 against the Chicago Bears. He missed one series while he was being fit for a brace, and said he surprised himself by feeling well enough to continue in the game. In each of his previous sprained MCLs, Jones said he missed the remainder of the game and then at least another two weeks.

On this occasion, with the Vikings out of trustworthy options, he returned to close out the game with a 15-yard run for a first down. Afterwards, he found his emotions swelling as he sought out O'Connell.

"I gave him hug and I was like, 'This s--- means something,'" Jones said. "This has been my life. This is what I came up on. So this is how I play."

Pro football is rife with military metaphors and associated hyperbole. In this case, Jones' effort and commitment genuinely moved people throughout the Vikings organization. His return in Chicago, and then his willingness to push through residual soreness to play the next three games, left the normally loquacious O'Connell in a rare spot.

"It's hard to even put into words," O'Connell said. "Just the toughness, the way he's been able to turn over after a high volume of carries and get to a place by the next Sunday with a lot of work, a lot of time in the recovery room and just knowing his body like he does. He's just been an absolute pro. He's been a warrior, and I'm just so thankful that we have Aaron Jones on our team."

Said offensive coordinator Wes Phillips: "The word 'warrior' has been thrown out many times, but it certainly highlights his toughness, his love for the game, and his commitment to this team and his teammates."

Jones split carries with teammates during much of his career with the Green Bay Packers, averaging 174 carries per season from 2017 to 2025. Were he to continue at his current rate this season, Jones would nearly double that average.

It almost certainly won't happen, given Mason's expected return, but Jones said he has demonstrated that even at this stage of his career, he can still provide credible games as a featured back. His 370 rushing yards during Mason's four-game absence were more than every NFL running back other than the Atlanta Falcons' Bijan Robinson (497) and the Buffalo Bills' James Cook (475).

"I feel like I showed that age is just a number," Jones said. "I take a lot of pride in knowing that they were counting on me, and then just showing that, 'Hey, I can still be an every-down productive back given the circumstances or given the opportunity.'"

It all bubbled to the surface in Week 5. Upset about a red zone fumble in the fourth quarter, he bulldozed over Saints safety Julian Blackmon and scored an 8-yard touchdown in fourth quarter to give the Vikings a 20-13 lead. He abandoned plans to perform a choreographed New Orleans-style dance and just let loose with a raw expression of emotion.

"I feel like it was a culmination of four weeks of work," he said, "along with answering and overcoming that fumble. It was a straight passion. I blacked out and started screaming, yelling, beating my chest.

"It was funny because after the game a couple of my buddies called me. They're from New Orleans. I played with them in college and they're like, 'Hey, we thought you were going to do a dance.' And I'm like, 'Bro, I blacked out. I just blacked out.'"

text:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Carolina Panthers coach Dave Canales said Wednesday that the team is preparing to host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday without top outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips.

Canales didn't offer a timeline for Phillips (hamstring) to return, but he avoided any gamesmanship on Phillips' status for Week 7.

When asked if the expectation was that Phillips would miss this week, with a "Thursday Night Football" matchup against the Green Bay Packers on deck for Week 8, Canales noted that Phillips, who reinjured his left hamstring in the road win over the Philadelphia Eagles, needed to be treated with caution.

"I think I can fairly say that," Canales said about Phillips missing Week 7. "I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of."

Phillips left Sunday's win in the first half but returned late in the third quarter. On Wednesday, Phillips walked around the perimeter of the Panthers' practice field while his teammates participated in a walkthrough.

"Jaelan got that same hamstring [injury] -- we've got to take care of that now," Canales said. "So, we're going to still push it and evaluate him, but this is something we're going to have to be smart with. Two weeks off of the first injury and then he was able to finish the game, which was incredible for him to go back out there and do his job. But the MRIs, the findings, this is something that we're going to have to treat more intensively."

Phillips, who signed a four-year, $120 million deal in March, has produced 2.5 sacks on the season. The former Miami Dolphins and Eagles pass rusher was brought in, along with inside linebacker Devin Lloyd, to turn around a middling Carolina defense.

But this Sunday, like Lloyd in Week 3's loss to the Cleveland Browns, Phillips will need to watch from the sideline as he recovers from injury.

Canales declined to speculate whether Phillips would be able to play at Green Bay next week. For now, though, with Phillips and special teams ace Thomas Incoom (calf) sidelined, the Panthers plan to call up practice squad linebacker Nick Hampton. The former Los Angeles Rams pass rusher is known for his special teams ability, and he recently returned to the Panthers after being cut with an undisclosed injury during training camp

"It's the reason why we brought him back, and he was having a great camp before he had the injury," Canales said. "So, we're excited to see Nick this week, and then some of the other guys that we've been working with, they've got to be ready if we go that direction with more guys."

Incoom, according to Canales, is considered week-to-week and won't be immediately placed on injured reserve. Incoom was injured against the Eagles, and Canales said it took four players to fill his role on special teams throughout the remainder of the Week 6 win.

Along with Phillips and Incoom, running back Chuba Hubbard, right tackle Taylor Moton, and tight ends Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller were given veteran rest days. Running back AJ Dillon (ankle) and offensive tackle Monroe Freeling (knee) were full participants after missing the previous week of practice and the win over the Eagles.

Denver Broncos running back Jonah Coleman (ankle) returned to practice on Wednesday as the team designated the rookie as a candidate to return from injured reserve.

Coleman has now opened his 21-day window to be activated to the 53-man roster. If he is not activated within three weeks, Coleman will remain on IR for the rest of the season. NFL teams are allowed to designate up to eight players to return from IR each season.

Coleman's return to practice comes at a good time for Denver as Tyler Badie just went down with a thumb injury last week.

Coleman (5-8, 220 pounds) was picked by the Broncos in the fourth round of this year's NFL draft out of Washington. He rushed 10 times for 39 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 while adding three receptions for 19 yards. Most of that production came after Coleman injured his ankle, but the severity of his injury was not known until after the game. After landing on IR, Coleman was required to sit out at least four games.

The rookie is now getting closer to returning as the club's RB3 behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. We'll see if he's officially activated to the 53-man roster ahead of Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.

text:
HOUSTON -- Texans wide receiver Tank Dell is ready to be tackled in his first game in nearly two years.

Dell, who has been out since he suffered a gruesome knee injury in December 2024, will make his return Sunday against the New York Giants. And he made it clear he is not afraid.

"I know it's a lot of questions, like, 'How he gonna look when he gets tackled?'" Dell said. "I don't care about none of that. I'm ready to get tackled. I'm gonna be joyful. Y'all gonna see the passion I have after I had that first catch."

Sunday will mark Dell's first game since he sustained multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap in the Texans' Week 16 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Dec. 21, 2024.

It has been almost 22 months since he has appeared in a game, but he said he is grateful to even be in position to play again.

"I'm blessed," Dell said. "I want to thank God for getting me back in this position. But I don't think I'm overwhelmed. I'm anxious, of course, but I don't think I'm overwhelmed. I'm anxious to get back out there and play some football."

A third-round pick in 2023, Dell started the 2026 season on injured reserve when Houston made its 53-man roster cuts even though he practiced throughout training camp. He took part only in individual drills throughout the summer because he wasn't fully ready for contact. He said Wednesday that he felt he was back to his old self last month.

Dell returns to a crowded Texans wideouts room, which includes Nico Collins, Jaylin Noel, Xavier Hutchinson, Marvin Harrison Jr. and Kayshon Boutte. But coach DeMeco Ryans said he hasn't placed any expectations on Dell as far as the number of reps he receives. He is just focused on celebrating Dell's return.

"It's just getting Tank back out there after missing two years of football," Ryans said. "That's the main thing. Him just going out playing ball. I don't care how many reps he gets. But I'll have my Tank Dell jersey on."

title: Patriots injured reserve activations explained: Decisions await - NBC Sports Boston
description:
Five years later, that number doubled to two players, but in the COVID-impacted 2020 season, the number was unlimited.
Patriots have nine players other players on IR Even while excluding Bryant, the Patriots have nine other players on IR who are eligible to return.
The need for Hollins and Doubs is obvious, even though the Patriots entered the season with receiver being their deepest position.
And with the Patriots limping into their Week 7 game in Chicago, more injuries await in the coming dozen weeks.
Yet this is the reality for the 2026 Patriots, a team that seemingly can't get through a game without losing multiple key players.
text:
Once upon a time, not all that long ago, the NFL -- a sport with a 100 percent injury rate, a game featuring several concurrent car crashes taking place on every snap, a league where ambulances and paramedics are on hand at all times -- did not allow any players to return to an active roster if they were placed on injured reserve at any point during a season.

This was, of course, insane.

The rules changed in 2012, when teams could activate one player from IR, but that player had to be selected as "designated for return." Five years later, that number doubled to two players, but in the COVID-impacted 2020 season, the number was unlimited.

In 2022, a new rule was established: Eight players could return to a team from IR during a season, provided those players missed four games. That was good. Eight felt like a lot. Most times, it is.

For the 2026 Patriots, though, it is not.

With only 35 percent of the season gone, the Patriots have already activated three players off IR, and they have a small handful of players who presumably will be activated when they are healthy enough to play again. Yet with 11 games remaining, more players certainly will get hurt, so the team likely will have to make some decisions to not bring back some of those players on IR.

Patriots have used three IR activations

Because Brenden Schooler was on the non-football injury list rather than the PUP list, his activation counted as one of the eight allotted slots.

A.J. Brown spent the minimum four weeks on IR after suffering a high ankle sprain in Week 1, returning to the team last week against the Jets.

And though he is -- as of this writing -- still in his 21-day practice window, offensive tackle Marcus Bryant has been tabbed to return. With Will Campbell playing through a knee injury in Week 6 and Morgan Moses questionable for Week 7 with a foot injury, the Patriots do need more depth at the position, even with rookie Caleb Lomu filling in well thus far.

Patriots have nine players other players on IR

Even while excluding Bryant, the Patriots have nine other players on IR who are eligible to return. In a subjective ranking of importance, those players are:

WR Mack Hollins

WR Romeo Doubs

G Greg Van Roten

S Dell Pettus

FB Reggie Gilliam

LB Quintayvious Hutchins

LB Khalil Jacobs

G Mike Onwenu*

P Bryce Baringer

*Mike Onwenu would rank at or near the top of the list, but his broken ankle likely ended his season.

The need for Hollins and Doubs is obvious, even though the Patriots entered the season with receiver being their deepest position. Brown was gone in Week 1, and as soon as he returned in Week 6, Doubs was heading out. That leaves a receiving corps of DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams to complement Brown. Presuming both Hollins (calf) and Doubs (shoulder) get healthy, the Patriots will want both back on the field as soon as possible.

The need for Van Roten is, likewise, very apparent after the team suffered injuries to both starting guards last week against the Jets, with Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Ben Brown (knee) both getting hurt. Brown was already a third-stringer (behind Onwenu and Van Roten), which forced Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse into action from deep on the depth chart. They got by against the Jets, and they'll try to stay above water against the Bears on a short week, but they desperately need experience at guard moving forward. Van Roten suffered a thigh injury in Week 3, so his status bears watching sooner than later.

Assuming those three players -- Hollins, Doubs, and Van Roten -- end up being activated off IR, that would bring the Patriots to six of their eight spots. With just two spots remaining, the Patriots will have decisions to make.

Despite being a backup, Dell Pettus (ankle) ranks high on the list because the Patriots do not have much safety depth at all. Starters Kevin Byard and Craig Woodson are both questionable for Thursday night's game vs. the Bears, and Woodson has already missed a game this year. The team might be comfortable with Jaylen Reed/Mike Brown/Elliott Davison as backups, but if either Woodson or Byard have to miss time, Pettus would be their best option.

Gilliam, too, is another logical choice. That has less to do with his effectiveness in his four games played and more to do with the fact that the Patriots pursued him in free agency and likely envisioned a significant blocking role for him in the running game. Yet considering he only averaged 14.5 snaps per game, and considering Cameron Latu may be a suitable replacement as a blocker, perhaps the Patriots ultimately won't make the call to activate Gilliam.

Hutchins and Jacobs rank in the middle of the list for reasons similar to Pettus: a lack of depth at their respective positions. Yet with so many other players already needed, it would be a bit of a surprise for the Patriots to activate their seventh-round pass rusher (Hutchins) or undrafted linebacker (Jacobs) over them.

Baringer, who got hurt during the preseason finale, may be a victim of circumstance if he heals from his lower-body injury, just by virtue of playing an extremely replaceable position. Mitch Wishnowsky has filled in and has arguably performed better than Baringer, so the team really can't afford to use one of its eight spots on a punter.

The unknown future injuries

To reiterate, this is the NFL. Injuries are, unfortunately, inevitable. And with the Patriots limping into their Week 7 game in Chicago, more injuries await in the coming dozen weeks.

And while the team can't know which players will get hurt to varying degrees in that remaining time, they do have to consider the need to keep one or two of those IR spots available in the event that anyone from the group of Drake Maye, Christian Gonzalez, Milton Williams, any pass rusher, Rhamondre Stevenson, Hunter Henry, Eli Raridon, Will Campbell, Morgan Moses, Christian Elliss, Robert Spillane, or either starting safety needs a trip to IR.

Two more for postseason

This part is significant: Teams can activate two more players off IR in the postseason. So, in the very likely event that the Patriots activate eight players from IR during the season, and the nearly just-as-likely event that a player suffers an injury late in the season that requires an IR trip, the Patriots will be able to activate that player in the postseason.

They did that last season, after Hollins suffered a late-season injury that was later revealed to have been a lacerated spleen. He was activated off IR before the AFC Championship Game in Denver.

That, however, is a problem for another day. If the injuries continue to mount for New England the way they have already, then the postseason may be the farthest thing from the team's mind while trying to navigate the months of November and December.

Occasionally, teams need to weigh these kinds of decisions for IR activations at some point in a season. Typically, that's much later than Week 7. Yet this is the reality for the 2026 Patriots, a team that seemingly can't get through a game without losing multiple key players.

text:
The Philadelphia Eagles are not being disciplined for how they handled quarterback Jalen Hurts’ blood clots, a spokesperson for the NFL said.

The league said in a statement Tuesday that officials had been in contact with Eagles medical personnel and the Cleveland Clinic in London throughout the process of Hurts’ being treated.

“The league’s Chief Medical Officer, Dr. Allen Sills, arranges for medical resources with leading providers in every international market with approval from the NFL Players Association,” the league said. “Medical care for players is provided by club medical staff in coordination with independent doctors.”

The players association released a statement on Tuesday saying that the union was told there would be no review into Hurts’ medical care.

“Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred,” the NFLPA statement said. “Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward.”

NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said he would welcome the investigation when asked about the union’s statement at a press conference following the league’s annual fall meeting Wednesday in New York.

“That’s part of our processes, that’s fine,” Goodell said. “We have our chief medical officer has been through the protocols that were followed, so we welcome that.”

He was also asked whether international travel had an impact on the complications with Hurts’ blood clot. He said he was unaware of the travel to and from London being a factor, but noted that it was for the medical professionals to determine.

The commissioner praised the league for having “the greatest medical advisors” working on player health. Goodell said the league was comfortable with Hurts’ care based on what the chief medical officer has evaluated.

“The most important thing here is Jalen’s health, ultimately, in the future. He’s a wonderful young man, and not just a great player, but he’s he’s someone we all care deeply about,” Goodell said. So, I’m more worried about his health ultimately. But the protocols were followed.

Hurts is on injured reserve and expected to miss the rest of the season after a blood clot in his left calf traveled to his lungs. The Eagles and agent Nicole Lynn said Monday that Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli.

Hurts’ treatment involves blood thinners, and he will not be allowed to participate in any football activities until he is off them.

Hurts played in London against Jacksonville on Oct. 11, three days after he informed medical staff members of the injury after practice. Specialists in London initially diagnosed him with left calf superficial vein thrombosis.
